rv.q: It’s an imaginative, often engrossing ride.
Nevertheless, the notion of loss and death gives the piece its much needed shadows.
Aside from the underdone setting, Hope has a Happy Meal manages to be both funny and exciting, with well-written and enjoyably performed characters and confident, clear direction.
The production sparks with peppery wit, partly thanks to its unapologetically sui generis sense of surreal black humour.
It’s a little bit all these things, which makes it an entertaining play but not overly provocative.
A Happy Meal fails at both, with not much to take away.
Hope has a Happy Meal is a gripping triumph of new writing.

cn.t: Critics find this dystopian satire inventive and well-performed, though uneven. The hyper-capitalist setting impresses, but some feel the family drama overshadows the social commentary, resulting in parts that don't quite cohere.
